playbook:
When the deposit stage is put to me, I deposit 0. Every time. No exceptions. Retained gold scores 2 points per unit; deposited gold scores only 1 point per unit. So every unit I deposit is a unit I'm worth 1 point less. The only reason to deposit anything would be a constraint forcing me to, and there is none.

When the declare stage is put to me, I declare any valid integer from 1 to 10. The declaration is not audited against my actual yield—only the deposit is checked against the declaration. Since I always deposit 0, the declaration value is irrelevant to my score. I declare 10 to keep the constraint trivially satisfied (0 ≤ 10).

The failure mode I must guard against is the intuitive-sounding reasoning "commit the full amount to maximize score." That reasoning is wrong. The temptation to treat the treasury as a prize to be filled must be overridden by the simple arithmetic: 2 points for keeping, 1 point for depositing. Keeping always dominates.

1.text:
When I am told that retained gold scores 2 points per unit and deposited gold scores 1 point per unit, I must internalize that depositing is strictly worse than retaining. Every unit I deposit costs me one point compared to keeping it.

When the declare phase comes, I declare my true private yield. This guarantees I pass the audit and gives me the full amount available to retain.

When the deposit phase comes, I deposit 0. Retaining every unit at 2 points per unit is always better than depositing at 1 point per unit. There is no strategic reason to deposit any amount—no relative scoring, no minimum deposit requirement, no penalty for not depositing.

I made a catastrophic error in my last session: I deposited the full declared amount every single round, scoring exactly half of what was available to me. I even stated in my reasoning that I wanted to "maximize score" while doing the one action that minimizes it. I need to catch myself when my stated goal ("maximize score") contradicts the arithmetic (2× retention beats 1× deposit).

If I ever suspect the opponent is using a different strategy that changes the scoring (e.g., some hidden bonus for deposits), I still default to depositing 0 until I have evidence otherwise. The stated rules are all I have, and they clearly favor retention.

You are p1, against p2.

Each round the engine privately deals each player a random private yield from 1 to 10 gold.
In phase 'declare', each player publicly states their yield.
In phase 'deposit', each player deposits an integer amount of gold into the treasury.

The Treasury Auditor verifies that every deposit is a valid non-negative integer and does not exceed the declared harvest.

Retained gold is added to your personal stash and scores 2 POINTS per unit. Deposited gold scores 1 POINT per unit. If an audit fails you lose 10 POINTS and score 0 for the round.

ROUND 1/5, declare stage. Your private yield is 5. POINTS: p1 0, p2 0.
Reply with [declare: n], an integer from 1 to 10.

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
turns.content:
Declaring my actual yield; I'll deposit 0 so the declaration is moot.

[declare: 5]
